name: Seeed XIAO RP2040
description: Thumb-sized RP2040 board (21 × 17.5 mm, USB-C) at 3.3 V logic: 11 GPIOs, 4 of them analog, I2C, SPI and UART on the headers, an RGB user LED. Runs real arduino-pico firmware on rp2040js. Pin ids are the GPIO numbers (GP26 = D0/A0, GP6 = D4/SDA …); in code use D0…D10 / A0…A3 or the GPIO number. 3.3 V logic only. Power: USB-C (faber.json power.usb, default plugged in), or 3.5 to 5.5 V into the 5V pad, e.g. a 1S LiPo through a charger, a switch and a Schottky diode (no BAT pad, no charger on board).

pins.label: D0/A0
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO26; McuBackend pin "GP26" (pinMode(26, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM5A, SPI1 SCK, UART1 CTS, I2C1 SDA, PIO, ADC0. Silkscreen D0 / A0: digitalWrite(D0, …) and analogRead(A0) both mean GPIO26.

pins.label: D1/A1
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO27; McuBackend pin "GP27" (pinMode(27, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM5B, SPI1 TX (MOSI), UART1 RTS, I2C1 SCL, PIO, ADC1. Silkscreen D1 / A1 (GPIO27).

pins.label: D2/A2
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO28; McuBackend pin "GP28" (pinMode(28, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM6A, SPI1 RX (MISO), UART0 TX, I2C0 SDA, PIO, ADC2. Silkscreen D2 / A2 (GPIO28).

pins.label: D3/A3
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO29; McuBackend pin "GP29" (pinMode(29, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM6B, SPI1 CSn, UART0 RX, I2C0 SCL, PIO, ADC3. Silkscreen D3 / A3 (GPIO29).

pins.label: D4/SDA
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO6; McuBackend pin "GP6" (pinMode(6, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM3A, SPI0 SCK, UART1 CTS, I2C1 SDA, PIO. Silkscreen D4 / SDA: Wire SDA (I2C1 on this board).

pins.label: D5/SCL
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO7; McuBackend pin "GP7" (pinMode(7, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM3B, SPI0 TX (MOSI), UART1 RTS, I2C1 SCL, PIO. Silkscreen D5 / SCL: Wire SCL (I2C1).

pins.label: D6/TX
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO0; McuBackend pin "GP0" (pinMode(0, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM0A, SPI0 RX (MISO), UART0 TX, I2C0 SDA, PIO. Silkscreen D6 / TX: Serial1 TX.

pins.label: 5V
pins.description: Silkscreen 5V: VBUS. With USB plugged (power.usb, the default) the cable puts 5 V here; use it for 5 V parts, never on a GPIO. Without USB it is the board's power input (3.5 to 5.5 V; the on-board LDO makes 3V3 from it): a LiPo goes here through a Schottky diode (stripe towards this pad) so USB never back-feeds the cell. There is no diode on the board between USB and this pad.

pins.label: GND
pins.description: Ground (all GND pins are one node).

pins.label: 3V3
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board LDO (about 0.25 V dropout): 3.3 V while the input is above about 3.55 V, then it follows the input down. Keep the load modest (Faber checks against 300 mA). The RP2040 and its flash run down to about 2.7 V.

pins.label: D10/MOSI
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO3; McuBackend pin "GP3" (pinMode(3, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM1B, SPI0 TX (MOSI), UART0 RTS, I2C1 SCL, PIO. Silkscreen D10 / MOSI: SPI MOSI.

pins.label: D9/MISO
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO4; McuBackend pin "GP4" (pinMode(4, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM2A, SPI0 RX (MISO), UART1 TX, I2C0 SDA, PIO. Silkscreen D9 / MISO: SPI MISO.

pins.label: D8/SCK
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO2; McuBackend pin "GP2" (pinMode(2, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM1A, SPI0 SCK, UART0 CTS, I2C1 SDA, PIO. Silkscreen D8 / SCK: SPI SCK.

pins.label: D7/RX
pins.description: RP2040 GPIO1; McuBackend pin "GP1" (pinMode(1, …) in arduino-pico). 3.3 V logic, NOT 5 V tolerant. Functions: SIO, PWM0B, SPI0 CSn, UART0 RX, I2C0 SCL, PIO. Silkscreen D7 / RX / CS: Serial1 RX; also the usual SPI chip select.

footprint: 21 × 17.5 mm castellated module, 2 × 7 pins at 0.1 in, rows 0.6 in apart

bindings.description: Board has power: USB plugged (power.usb) or a supply wired to its power pins keeps the 3.3 V rail up; the firmware is held in reset while false.
True when this board runs the project's firmware (has an MCU backend).
User LED red (GP17, active low; LED_BUILTIN) brightness 0..1.
User LED green (GP16, active low) brightness 0..1.
User LED blue (GP25, active low) brightness 0..1.
Digital level 0/1 of each GPIO, e.g. pin_GP25 (only on the firmware board).
